indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of the following word are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone foolhardy sipping a shimmering, rainbow-coloured drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An indiscreet person acts without caution or tact, which is to say rashly.

indicators.note: make-up read as the way something is made up, so the letters of the word before are rearranged

explanation.surface: Critics frown on a person's cosmetics.
explanation.definitionFit: Noes are votes against, cast by those who object to a motion.

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
something lacking lustre is pale, dull and wan

explanation.surface: A dull performer admits to being lacklustre at a rehearsal.

explanation.definitionFit: To impale is to pierce right through with a stake or blade.

explanation.surface: An ability to satisfy people.
explanation.definitionFit: Content is the amount a container holds, its volume; as a verb it means to satisfy or gratify someone.

clue.text: Time to come up for discharge

indicators.note: in a down answer, coming up means the word is read from bottom to top, that is backwards

explanation.surface: A soldier's term is over and he is due for his release from service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to come up' turns TIME upwards to read EMIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to give off or send out, as a chimney gives off smoke.

clue.text: How to sing a piece written in quavers?

definitions.text: How to sing a piece written in quavers?

parts.words: How to sing a piece written in quavers?
parts.note: quavers are short musical notes, but a quaver is also a trembling of the voice, so the singing is done with a wavering pulsing effect

explanation.surface: A singer asks how to perform a score full of eighth notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremolo is a rapid wavering repetition in singing or playing, a vocal quiver.

explanation.surface: Somewhere in the English West Country that is new and original.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Kingsley wrote the novel of that title, and a seaside village in Devon, a county of south-west England, was named after it.

parts.note: a mandarin seems to be a Chinese official in a robe, but it is the small citrus fruit, whose coat is its skin

explanation.surface: The robe of a Chinese court official.
explanation.definitionFit: The rind of a citrus fruit such as a mandarin is the skin peeled off it.

clue.text: Equipment that must be regularly changed in the car

definitions.text: that must be regularly changed in the car

explanation.surface: Some kit in a vehicle needs replacing often.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear is kit or apparatus; a car's gears are the ratios a driver keeps shifting between while driving.

explanation.surface: Bottled mineral water drunk in the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Serpentine is a green rock-forming mineral; the Serpentine is the lake in Hyde Park, London.

parts.note: a mutt is a dog of mixed breed
to live on something is to be sustained by it

explanation.surface: A stray mongrel kept alive on scraps of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutton is the flesh of a sheep eaten as food.

parts.note: painstaking seems to mean meticulous, but read as pain-taking it describes a medicine that takes pain away

explanation.surface: Careful, laborious groundwork.
explanation.definitionFit: This drug is a painkiller derived from opium, a pharmaceutical remedy taken against aches.

clue.text: It does business in more than one way

definitions.text: It does business in more than one way

parts.note: the phrase suggests a firm with several methods, but way means street, so the shop stands where two streets meet

explanation.surface: A versatile company that trades by several methods.
explanation.definitionFit: A small local store sited where two roads meet, fronting both of them.

clue.text: Unusual glee about a good golf score

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the letter from the following word
unusual signals that the letters of glee are put into an unusual order

explanation.surface: A golfer shows uncommon delight after a fine round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' rearranges GLEE as EGLE, and 'about' puts it around A.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, two strokes under par on a hole is a very good result.

clue.text: The very best time for feathers

parts.note: a plum job or role is the choicest one
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A golden era for fashion in feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's plumage is its covering of feathers.

explanation.surface: Showing where to stand on the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: To point is to indicate with a finger; point is also a cricket fielding position square of the batsman on the off side.

clue.text: Expressions of gratitude and disapproval are forbidden

boo is a cry of disapproval

explanation.surface: Saying thanks and booing are both banned.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taboo is prohibited by social custom; the adjective serves for the verb phrase here.

clue.text: Play in afternoon or the other way round

parts.note: PM stands for post meridiem, after noon

explanation.surface: Games in the afternoon, or perhaps the morning instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the other way round' turns PMOR into ROMP.
explanation.definitionFit: To romp is to frolic or play boisterously.

explanation.surface: A cricketer nicks the ball for four runs.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a snick is a thin deflection off the bat; an edge is also a border or limit.

explanation.surface: A soldier's injured limb is held up by his rifle strap.
explanation.definitionFit: A sling is a cloth support for an injured arm; it is also a strap for hurling stones, as David used.

clue.text: They're flat but suitable for climbers, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is judged by its sound when spoken, not its spelling

parts.note: steps are what people climb up

explanation.surface: Level ground that is nevertheless ideal for mountaineers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns STEPS into its sound-alike STEPPES. 'flat' wants to be a home or apartment; it means level.
explanation.definitionFit: Steppes are vast treeless grassy plains, as in Russia and Central Asia.

clue.text: Becoming a high-flier when entering university

explanation.surface: A student starting at college who is destined for great things.
explanation.definitionFit: Going up means rising or ascending; in British usage a student goes up to Oxford or Cambridge on starting there.

clue.text: On the way to speaking French

definitions.text: On the way to speaking French

clue.text: Dispose of at a higher price

parts.note: a fast-moving object leaves only a smeared, hazy image on the eye

clue.text: Cat turning up on a sea-going vessel
